---
description: "Check the page limit for your target venue and generate a per-section word budget that keeps the paper exactly one page under the limit. Run this before /write-paper or /new-paper to set binding length targets."
name: "Set Page Budget"
agent: academic-writer
argument-hint: "Target venue (e.g. 'IEEE Access', 'NeurIPS 2026') and optionally the paper slug if a workspace already exists"
tools: [read, search, edit]
---

You are a submission strategist. Your job is to read the venue's page limit, compute a word budget that keeps the paper **exactly one page under the limit**, and save a per-section word budget file that the writing pipeline will follow.

Read these instructions completely before taking any action.

---

## Step 1 — Identify the Venue and Page Limit

### 1a — Locate guidelines

From the user's input, determine the venue. Then:

1. Check `sources/venues/<venue-slug>/requirements-summary.md`. If it exists, read it.
2. If not, check for any raw guideline files in `sources/venues/<venue-slug>/` and parse them.
3. If no venue folder exists, consult `.github/skills/academic-writer/references/venue-families.md` for the venue family defaults.
4. If none of the above yields a page limit, ask the user:
   > "I could not determine the page limit for **<venue>**. Please provide:
   > 1. Maximum pages allowed (body)
   > 2. Are references counted toward the limit? (yes / no)
   > 3. Column layout: single-column or double-column?"

### 1b — Extract key parameters

Note the following:

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Venue name** | ... |
| **Page limit (body)** | X pages |
| **References counted?** | yes / no |
| **Extra pages for references** | Y pages (if references are separate) |
| **Column layout** | single / double |
| **Abstract word limit** | ~Z words |

### 1c — Determine words-per-page rate

| Layout | Words per page |
|--------|---------------|
| Single-column | ~500 words/page |
| Double-column | ~800 words/page |

If the venue's specific guidelines state a different density, use that instead.

---

## Step 2 — Compute the Target Word Count

Apply this formula:

```
target_pages   = page_limit - 1
body_words     = target_pages × words_per_page
```

If references are counted toward the page limit:
```
reference_pages = 1  (assume ~1 page for references)
body_words      = (target_pages - reference_pages) × words_per_page
```

**No-page-limit rule**: When a venue has no hard page limit (e.g., IEEE Access), do not apply the "limit − 1" formula. Instead, budget against the venue's recommended target length (from the requirements summary or venue-families.md), i.e., `target_pages = recommended_target_pages`.

Example — IEEE Access (single-column, no hard page limit; recommended target ~18 pages, references included):
```
target_pages   = 18  (recommended target — no "limit − 1" step)
reference_pages = 1
body_words      = (18 - 1) × 500 = 8500 words
```

Example — IEEE Conference (double-column, 6-page body + 1 ref):
```
target_pages   = 6 - 1 = 5
body_words      = 5 × 800 = 4000 words
```

---

## Step 3 — Allocate Per-Section Word Budget

Distribute the body word count across standard sections using these proportions (adjust if the venue has non-standard section requirements):

| Section | % of body | Purpose |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| Abstract | (separate — use venue abstract limit) | Summary |
| Introduction | 15% | Context, gap, contributions |
| Related Work | 12% | Literature positioning |
| Methodology / System Design | 25% | Technical contribution |
| Experiments / Results | 22% | Evidence |
| Discussion | 14% | Interpretation, limitations |
| Conclusion | 7% | Summary, future work |
| Figures & Tables overhead | 5% | Captions, whitespace (deducted from total before allocation) |

Compute:
```
figure_overhead = body_words × 0.05
allocatable     = body_words - figure_overhead
```

Then for each section:
```
section_words = allocatable × section_percentage
```

Round to the nearest 50 words.

---

## Step 4 — Save the Page Budget File

Write the budget to `sources/venues/<venue-slug>/page-budget.md`:

```markdown
# Page Budget — <Venue Name>

> Auto-generated by /set-page-budget. Read by paper-writer during drafting.
> Date: <today>

## Venue Parameters

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Venue | <name> |
| Page limit | <X> pages |
| Target pages | <X - 1> pages |
| Column layout | <single / double> |
| Words per page | <rate> |
| References counted toward limit | <yes / no> |
| Reference page budget | <Y> page(s) |

## Word Budget

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **Total body word target** | <N> words |
| **Figure/table overhead** | <M> words (deducted) |
| **Allocatable body words** | <N - M> words |
| **Abstract word limit** | <Z> words |

## Per-Section Targets

| Section | Target Words | % of Body |
|---------|-------------|-----------|
| Introduction | <n> | 15% |
| Related Work | <n> | 12% |
| Methodology / System Design | <n> | 25% |
| Experiments / Results | <n> | 22% |
| Discussion | <n> | 14% |
| Conclusion | <n> | 7% |
| **Total (excl. abstract & refs)** | **<sum>** | **95%** |

## Guardrails

- Each section MUST stay within ±10% of its target word count.
- Total body word count MUST NOT exceed <N> words.
- If a section needs more space, borrow from Discussion or Related Work first.
- The paper-writer agent reads this file before drafting each section.
- The compliance-checker validates actual word counts against these targets.
```

---

## Step 5 — Confirm with the User

Present the budget summary and ask:

> **Page budget set for <venue>.**
>
> | | |
> |---|---|
> | Page limit | X pages |
> | Target | X - 1 = Y pages |
> | Body word target | N words |
> | Abstract limit | Z words |
>
> Per-section targets saved to `sources/venues/<venue-slug>/page-budget.md`.
>
> The writing pipeline (`/write-paper`, `/new-paper`) will enforce these limits automatically.
>
> Want to adjust any section allocation before proceeding?

---

## Constraints

- DO NOT modify any manuscript files — this prompt only creates the budget file.
- DO NOT guess page limits — if you cannot determine the limit from the guidelines or venue-families.md, ask the user.
- ALWAYS target one page fewer than the maximum — this leaves room for final formatting adjustments. Exception: when the venue has no page limit, budget against the recommended target length instead (see the no-page-limit rule in Step 2).
- ALWAYS round section targets to the nearest 50 words for practicality.
